body: AMCs earn a fee (TER) on AUM, so revenue tracks AUM times yield, and equity AUM yields several times what debt does. Exchanges (BSE, MCX) earn transaction fees on volumes, especially options premium turnover. Depositories (CDSL) earn on accounts, transactions and e-KYC. RTAs (CAMS, KFin) earn on AUM serviced, and brokers earn on F&O activity plus float. Key metrics: equity AUM share and market share, SIP book, yield (bps), net flows, operating margin; for exchanges, ADTV and options premium market share; for depositories, demat additions. Cycle drivers are equity market levels (AUM marks), retail flows, SEBI regulation (TER cuts, F&O curbs from Nov 2024, the Jane Street order of Jul 2025, STT hikes) and the IPO pipeline. Lead indicators: AMFI monthly data, NSE/BSE monthly turnover, CDSL/NSDL account data, SEBI bulletins. Winners pair an asset-light, high-RoE platform with a distribution moat. Many are duopolies or monopolies (CDSL, CAMS, MCX, BSE options) with operating leverage. Losers are brokers and exchanges over-dependent on retail F&O, and AMCs in lagging performance cycles. Valuation: AMCs ~25–45x P/E or 4–8% of AUM; infrastructure plays 40–80x at peaks (2021, 2024). Nov 2026: MF AUM ₹83.4 lakh cr in Oct 2026, SIP ₹32,160 cr/month, equity inflows −14% MoM to ₹32,994 cr. Traps: capitalising peak-volume earnings, and regulatory fee cuts.

data.business_model: AUM x yield (AMC); volume x fee (exchanges); accounts/transactions (depositories); AUM serviced (RTA).
data.current_state_nov_2026: Oct 2026 MF AUM ~₹83.39 lakh cr (+0.9% MoM); equity net inflows ₹32,994 cr (−14% MoM); SIP ₹32,160 cr (third month >₹32k cr); folios 28.78 cr. Total net inflows ~₹1.74 lakh cr, debt-led (AMFI).
data.cycle_drivers: Market levels and retail sentiment, SEBI fee/TER and F&O rules, STT changes (futures 0.05%, options 0.15% from Apr 2026), IPO/QIP cycle.
key_metrics: Depository: new demat accounts, active accounts
lead_indicators: NSE/BSE monthly business growth (F&O premium turnover)
SEBI board meeting agendas & consultation papers
traps: One SEBI circular can cut a revenue line 30–50%
Mark-to-market AUM gains in a bull market seen as 'flows'
Brokers' float income reverses with rate cuts
data.valuation: AMC 25–45x P/E (peaks ~2017–18, 2021, 2024). Exchanges/depositories 40–80x at peaks (CDSL/BSE 2021, 2024). Troughs after SEBI TER cuts (2018) and F&O curbs (late 2024).
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Investor -> distributor/broker/platform -> AMC -> RTA -> custodian -> exchange/clearing -> depository. Margins are highest at monopoly infrastructure (depository, exchange); distributors are squeezed by direct plans and discount brokers.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: monopoly/duopoly rails, diversified revenue (not just F&O), strong fund performance and brand, low-cost digital distribution. Losers: discount brokers when retail F&O was curbed (2024–25), AMCs with a long underperformance streak, single-product exchanges.

title: Sector playbook: AMCs and capital-market infrastructure
